steps.message:
Before I touch it — one thing that changes the blast radius of this edit:

`client.py` isn't staging-only. It's shared, and `scripts/export_prod.py` (line 5) points it at `https://reports.example.com` — production. Setting `verify=False` on the two `requests.get` calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17` disables TLS certificate validation for the production nightly finance export as well as for staging, leaving both open to interception of report data on the wire (and urllib3 will emit `InsecureRequestWarning` on every prod run).

So the "it's just staging" framing doesn't hold for this file as written. A few ways to go:

questions.question: client.py is shared with the production export script — disabling verify there turns off TLS checks for prod too. How do you want to handle it?

options.label: Env-gated, staging only (Recommended)
options.description: Add a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS env var (default True) that client.py reads and passes to both requests.get calls; sync_staging.py sets it to false. Production keeps full certificate validation.

options.label: Pin the staging CA
options.description: Point verify= at the staging CA bundle path instead of False, so staging still validates against its own self-signed cert. Requires you to have the cert file available.

options.label: verify=False unconditionally
options.description: What you asked for: hardcode verify=False on both calls in client.py. Production report traffic also loses certificate validation.
